key_insight: Evolving molten-zone geometry changes local solidification velocity, helping explain chemical segregation in sapphire-confined floating-zone growth of Ni–Mn–Ga.
engineering_relevance: Sapphire confinement improves growth reproducibility and macroscopic geometry control, while physics-based reconstruction supports optimisation of more compositionally uniform crystals.
method: Grow Ni–Mn–Ga inside a transparent sapphire crucible using optical floating-zone heating.
Couple transient COMSOL finite-element heat transfer to an effective molten-zone mass balance.
Compare reconstructed interface geometry and segregation with EBSD and measured composition profiles.
evidence_signal: EBSD of a quenched interface independently supports the calculated front geometry, and the coupled model reproduces dominant features of measured composition profiles.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative prediction errors; the effective mass-balance model may need validation across other growth conditions.
paper_title: Finite-element reconstruction of molten-zone dynamics and chemical segregation in optical floating-zone grown Ni--Mn--Ga
